# 45 Recto

The Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, and Sadhyas; the Vishvedevas, the two Ashvins, the Maruts, and the <term>Ushmapas</term> <gloss>ancestors who drink the steam or warmth of offerings</gloss>; groups of Gandharvas, Yakshas, Asuras, and Siddhas; they all gaze upon you in amazement. <note>original: "rudrādityā vasavo ye ca sādhyā..." - Bhagavad Gita 11.22</note>

Seeing your vast form with many mouths and eyes, O mighty-armed one, with many arms, thighs, and feet, many bellies, and many terrible tusks, the worlds are terrified, and so am I. <note>original: "rūpaṃ mahat te bahuvaktranetraṃ..." - Bhagavad Gita 11.23</note>

Touching the sky, glowing with many colors, with mouths wide open and large shining eyes, seeing you, my inner soul trembles. I find neither steadiness nor peace, O Vishnu. <note>original: "nabhaḥspṛśaṃ dīptam anekavarṇaṃ..." - Bhagavad Gita 11.24</note>

Seeing your mouths with terrible tusks, resembling the fire of destruction <term>kalanalasannibhani</term> <gloss>like the fire that consumes the universe at the end of time</gloss>...

---

# 45 Verso

...distinguished by the night, the people will not live, nor will they be joyful. Here is the glorious abode, the eternal servant, fame without the gods <unclear>atra sudhama sadasa kirti vina vina sura</unclear>. In the gathering of the slow-moving ones, the joy of the enemies <unclear>arivahalananda</unclear>. The eternal servant, fame without the gods. The priest <term>Bhatta</term> <gloss>learned scholar or priest</gloss> has reached the sleep of the cardinal directions, all of them terrible. Fame without the gods.

Then through the sacrifice <term>yajnena</term> <gloss>ritual offering</gloss>... <note>verse 21</note> Just as the bringer of joy, the glorious abode <unclear>yathanandinaya rudhama</unclear>. <note>verse 22</note> Here is the glorious abode, the eternal servant, fame without the gods.

The winds and the great ones are broad and glorious, like the forest <unclear>dhavamananana dayo yavishalinaja thasibhilanalı</unclear>. <note>verse 23</note> Here is the glorious abode, the eternal servant, fame without the gods.

<note>A medium-sized circular hole is carved into the center of the palm leaf to allow a cord to pass through for binding the manuscript together.</note>

<summary>This page continues the revelation of the Universal Form where Arjuna describes the various deities and spirits witnessing the divine manifestation. The text expresses Arjuna's overwhelming fear and loss of composure upon seeing the destructive aspect of the deity.</summary>
<keywords>Vishwarupa, Universal Form, Vishnu, Arjuna, Rudras, Adityas, cosmic fire, divine revelation, palm leaf manuscript</keywords>
